players.product: Helios rack-scale platform (Instinct + EPYC, Infinity Fabric / UALink scale-up)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jean Hu on Q2 2026: the sixth consecutive quarter of greater than 30% year-over-year revenue growth; revenue up 13% sequentially; on a comparable basis diluted EPS up approximately 82% YoY. Gross margin expanded to 56%, up over 200 basis points YoY and 80 basis points sequentially on product mix and a growing data center contribution. Operating expenses $3.4 billion (+40% YoY) as AMD invests in R&D for AI silicon, systems and software; operating income $3.1 billion, a 27% operating margin. Segment operating income: Data Center $2.1 billion (31% of revenue); Client and Gaming $582 million (15%) versus $767 million (21%) a year ago; Embedded $386 million (40%) versus $275 million (33%). Cash from continuing operations $2.4 billion, free cash flow $1.6 billion; inventory rose sequentially to approximately $8.5 billion to support strong data center demand.
quarterly_data.figure: GM 56%; opex $3.4B (+40%); operating income $3.1B (27%); Embedded operating income $386M (40%); FCF $1.6B; inventory ~$8.5B

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jean Hu on the Q3 2026 outlook by segment: year over year, very strong double-digit growth in Data Center, strong double-digit growth in Embedded, and a decline in Client and Gaming (Client growth more than offset by a significant double-digit decline in Gaming). Sequentially revenue up approximately 13%, with strong double-digit growth in both Data Center and Embedded and a modest Client and Gaming decline (slight Client growth offset by a strong double-digit Gaming decline). Non-GAAP operating expenses approximately $3.65 billion and a 13% non-GAAP effective tax rate. CEO Lisa Su: 'we think Q3 is certainly a strong quarter ... and in Q4, it will be higher than that', with the Helios ramp 'just starting at the end of Q3' and 'much more substantial in Q4'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue up ~13% QoQ; non-GAAP opex ~$3.65B; tax rate 13%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jean Hu on 2027 gross margin: 'our gross margin is primarily driven by the business mix' — the expanding server business is accretive to overall gross margin, while data center AI adds large revenue and gross profit 'even though the gross margin is slightly below corporate average'; 'I think the mix will determine how we go through 2027'; the recovering embedded business 'will give us additional tailwind on the gross margin side in 2027', and client will also continue to improve gross margin. On spending: 'You should expect us to manage this OpEx increase less than the top-line revenue growth.'

Client and Gaming, CEO Lisa Su: Ryzen PRO sales grew more than 50% YoY with new wins at large healthcare, technology, automotive and financial services companies; Dell, HP, Lenovo, Asus and others launched commercial PCs on Ryzen AI PRO 400 Series processors; Ryzen AI Halo developer systems went on sale in the quarter, and the next-generation Ryzen AI Halo platform (Gorgon Halo processor) offers 192 gigabytes of unified memory and runs models with up to 300 billion parameters; AMD is partnering with Hugging Face to include one year of Hugging Face Pro with every Ryzen AI Halo system beginning later this year. AMD is 'planning for a softer PC market' in H2 'as higher memory and component costs weigh on demand' but expects client to perform better than the market and to grow in 2026 YoY. Gaming revenue fell 31% YoY to $779 million on lower semi-custom sales at this stage of the console cycle; higher industry-wide component costs raised graphics card prices and weighed on demand.
quarterly_data.figure: Ryzen PRO +>50% YoY; Gorgon Halo 192 GB unified memory, up to 300B-parameter models; Gaming $779M (-31%)

quarterly_data.signal: Embedded, CEO Lisa Su: revenue up 19% YoY to $977 million, the strongest growth in more than three years, on networking, aerospace and defense, test measurement and emulation, and communications customers. The embedded x86 business grew significantly 'as hyperscalers and networking customers increasingly adopted our CPUs to power critical networking and control plane functions in the data center'. New products: Ryzen AI Embedded X100 processors for real-time edge AI and the Kria AI robotics platform for physical AI. AMD is 'tracking towards another record year with more than $18 billion of new design wins', led by networking, data center, communications, test, and aerospace and defense customers; embedded semi-custom engagements are expanding.
quarterly_data.figure: Embedded $977M (+19%); >$18B new design wins tracked for the year

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Lisa Su: 'With Venice and MI450X now in production, initial Helios shipments set to begin this quarter'. CFO Jean Hu: Data Center segment revenue 'was a record $6.7 billion, more than doubling year-over-year and up 16% sequentially.'

quarterly_data.signal: Instinct, Q2 2026: CFO Jean Hu — Instinct sales more than doubled YoY 'with the continued ramp of our Instinct MI350 Series of products as adoption broadened across the largest AI labs, cloud providers, leading AI startups, national labs, and the sovereign AI deployment'. CEO Lisa Su — MI355X adoption continued to broaden as leading AI companies scaled deployments across inferencing and training workloads, and cloud providers expanded MI350 series availability; the growing number and scale of Helios and MI450 Series deployments 'position the business for significant growth in the second half of the year, with growth accelerating in 2027'.

players.product: EPYC Turin (Zen 5) server CPU silicon design

quarterly_data.signal: Server CPU cadence and upside, CEO Lisa Su: 'we believe that the server CPU is going to grow substantially in Q3 and in Q4', with more supply coming on for server in Q4; on the >70% 2027 server growth target: 'I believe, depending on how things play out, there may be opportunities for that growth to go higher as we get through the next few quarters.' AMD has been working across its supply chain — 'wafers, that's back-end capacity, that's substrates' — and sees 'much more capacity coming in line in 2027'. Hyperscalers and cloud providers keep expanding EPYC: healthcare, financial services, media and technology companies added tens of millions of EPYC cloud instances in the quarter.

Customer Lenovo: named by CEO Lisa Su among the OEMs with fifth-gen EPYC platforms in market — 'More than 230 5th-gen EPYC platforms are now in market from HPE, Dell, Lenovo, Supermicro, and others, our broadest enterprise portfolio to date.'
